{{Short description|Genus of anyklosaurian dinosaur}} {{Speciesbox | fossil_range = [[Late Cretaceous]], {{fossilrange|Cenomanian|Cenomanian|late [[Cenomanian]]}} | image = Nipponopelta holotype FPDM.png | image_caption = Replica of holotype specimen displayed at the [[Fukui Prefectural Dinosaur Museum]] | display_parents = 2 | genus = Nipponopelta | parent_authority = Oyabu et al., [[2026 in archosaur paleontology|2026]] | species = yezoensis | authority = Oyabu et al., 2026 }} '''''Nipponopelta''''' ({{lit|Japanese shield}}) is an [[extinct]] genus of [[nodosaurid]] ankylosaurian dinosaur known from the [[Upper Cretaceous]] ([[Cenomanian]] age) [[Hikagenosawa Formation]] of the [[Yezo Group]] in Japan. The genus contains a [[Monotypic taxon|single species]], '''''Nipponopelta yezoensis''''', known from a partial skull and fragmentary associated remains. It is the first ankylosaur to be named from Japan. == Discovery and naming == [[File:Nipponopelta yezoensis.png|thumb|[[Life restoration]]]] The ''Nipponopelta'' fossil material was discovered by Eijiro Goto on June 25, 1995, along the bank of the Omakizawa River in the city of [[Yūbari, Hokkaido|Yūbari]] in [[Hokkaido]], Japan. The partial skull of an ankylosaur was preserved within a [[calcareous]] [[concretion]] that had eroded from outcrops of the Hikagenosawa Formation. Goto donated the fossil to the [[Mikasa City Museum]], where it was permanently [[Accession number (cultural property)|accessioned]] as specimen MCM A522. It was [[prepared]] using [[formic acid]] to dissolve some of the surrounding rock. Preparation was halted after isolated, disarticulated teeth were found in the skull's cavities, to maintain the specimen's structural stability. In 1996, Hiroshi Hayakawa and [[Kenneth Carpenter]] preliminarily reported on the new specimen in a [[conference abstract]] for the Annual Meeting of the Palaeontological Society of Japan. In 2005, Hayakawa, Makoto Manabe, and Carpenter published a more detailed description of the specimen. They noted that much of the fossil remained encased in the matrix, obscuring many of the anatomical details. The material they could observe included the rear portion of the skull (the front part being missing), several disarticulated teeth, the [[Atlas (anatomy)|atlas]] (first [[cervical vertebra]]), and two [[osteoderm]]s (armor plates). Based on the {{dinogloss|fenestra|skull fenestration}} pattern and the structure of the [[occipital condyle]] and teeth, they identified it as a member of the [[ankylosaur]] clade [[Nodosauridae]]. In 2026, Shumpei Oyabu and colleagues [[Species description|described]] ''Nipponopelta yezoensis'' as a new genus and species of nodosaurid ankylosaur based on these fossil remains, designating MCM A522 as the [[holotype]] specimen. Using [[CT scan]]s of the fossil, they were able to identify previously unrecognized anatomical features, including two complete teeth, the left [[semicircular canals]], and a small part of the left [[mandible]]. The [[Genus|generic name]], ''Nipponopelta'', combines the [[Japanese language|Japanese]] word [[:wikt:日本|日本]] ({{lang|ja|[[:wikt:nippon|Nippon]]}}), meaning {{gloss|Japan}}, with the [[Greek language|Greek]] word {{lang|grc|[[:wikt:πέλτη|πέλτη]]}} ({{lang|grc|[[:wikt:pelta|péltē]]}}), meaning {{gloss|shield}}. The [[Specific name (zoology)|specific name]], ''yezoensis'', alludes to Yezo, the traditional name for Hokkaido, where the only known specimen was discovered. The description of this species makes it the first ankylosaur to be named from Japan. == Classification == To test the affinities and relationships of ''Nipponopelta'', Oyabu et al. (2026) included it in an updated version of the [[phylogenetic]] matrix of Xing et al. (2024), which in turn was derived from Raven et al. (2023). ''Nipponopelta'' was recovered as a [[Basal (phylogenetics)|derived]] member of the [[Nodosauridae]], more closely related to ''[[Nodosaurus]]'' and ''[[Panoplosaurus]]'' ([[Nodosaurinae]]) than to ''[[Polacanthus]]'' ([[Polacanthinae]]) or ''[[Struthiosaurus]]'' ([[Struthiosauridae]]). The taxa closest to ''Nipponopelta'' were recovered in a large, unresolved [[polytomy]]. After removing several unstable "wildcard taxa" for improved resolution, their 50% majority-rule consensus tree recovered ''Nipponopelta'' as the [[sister taxon]] to ''[[Pawpawsaurus]]'', with ''[[Borealopelta]]'' and a ''[[Edmontonia longiceps]]'' + ''[[Denversaurus]]'' clade as successive sister branches. As such, ''Nipponopelta'' is much more closely related to North American nodosaurids than to Asian taxa, the closest of which, in their analyses, is the Chinese ''[[Taohelong]]''. This formation represents a marine [[depositional environment]]. In their description of this taxon, Oyabu and colleagues suggested that ''Nipponopelta'' and its close relatives favored near-marine settings like [[Marine coastal ecosystem|coastal]] and [[Estuary|estuarine]] environments. However, they acknowledged that the frequent occurrence of nodosaurid remains in marine deposits could be partially explained by post-mortem transport of carcasses. Nevertheless, various points of evidence, including [[Fossil track|fossil trackways]], indicate that many nodosaurids predominantly occupied lowland, fluvial, and coastal habitats, which may have played an important role in their [[Oceanic dispersal|dispersal between continents]]. == References == {{Reflist|refs= {{Cite journal |last1=Oyabu |first1=Shumpei |last2=Kobayashi |first2=Yoshitsugu |last3=Zelenitsky |first3=Darla K. |last4=Fiorillo |first4=Anthony R. |last5=Kano |first5=Manabu |date=2026-08-21 |title=A new nodosaurid ankylosaur (Dinosauria: Ornithischia) from the Upper Cretaceous Hikagenosawa Formation in Japan reveals dispersal pattern of Asian nodosaurid ankylosaurs |journal=[[Cretaceous Research]] |language=en |article-number=106477 |issue=in press |doi=10.1016/j.cretres.2026.106477}} {{Cite journal |last1=Hayakawa |first1=Hiroshi |last2=Manabe |first2=Makoto |last3=Carpenter |first3=Kenneth |date=March 2005 |title=Nodosaurid ankylosaur from the Cenomanian of Japan |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/pdf/4524434.pdf |journal=[[Journal of Vertebrate Paleontology]] |language=en |volume=25 |issue=1 |pages=240–245 |doi=10.1671/0272-4634(2005)025[0240:NAFTCO]2.0.CO;2 |jstor=4524434 |issn=0272-4634}} {{Cite journal |last1=Xing |first1=Lida |last2=Niu |first2=Kecheng |last3=Mallon |first3=Jordan |last4=Miyashita |first4=Tetsuto |date=2024-02-17 |title=A new armored dinosaur with double cheek horns from the early Late Cretaceous of southeastern China |journal=Vertebrate Anatomy Morphology Palaeontology |language=en |volume=11 |doi=10.18435/vamp29396 |issn=2292-1389|doi-access=free }} {{Cite journal |last1=Raven |first1=Thomas J. |last2=Barrett |first2=Paul M. |last3=Joyce |first3=Chris B. |last4=Maidment |first4=Susannah C.
